Improperly of a leader of an army

Thus I emended what is in M στρατὸν ὑποδώκει [he guided the army under (his foot)], changed by a second hand to εὐ ἐποδώκει [he guided well]. The scholiast says, ὑπὸ τὸν ἑαυτοῦ πόδα ἡνιόχει [he drove it under his own foot]. Tan. Faber Epist. 1, 67 p. 223 was closest to the truth in correcting to εὐ ἐποδόχει [he guided well], which should have been written εὐ ποδούχει [he guided well with his foot]. On the verb ποδουχεῖν [to guide with the foot], usually written ποδοχεῖν in the books, see the passages of grammarians collected in Thes. vol. 6 p. 1280 and in Philologus vol. 13 p. 486 487.

[The more probable reading is ποδωκείᾳ [swiftness of foot] (from the nominative proparoxytone ποδώκεια [swiftness of foot]), which I restored from the apograph Flor.; on which see Thes. vol. 6 p. 1281.]
